official.deadline_note: The 14:00 CEST cutoff on 23 October 2026 applies both to the application and to the two reference letters; references will not be accepted after the deadline and the online form is not active after that date.
official.status_note: The 2027-28 call is open; the online application form has been available since late July 2026 and closes on 23 October 2026 at 14:00 CEST.
benefits: One-year residential fellowship at the Robert Schuman Centre for Advanced Studies, Villa Schifanoia
Association with one of the Centre's projects and programmes
Active participation in the academic life of the Centre; fellows can take part in the activities of the EUI postdoctoral programme
Access to the Centre's seminar series, including the Schuman Seminar series and the annual Yves Meny Lecture
EUI assistance to non-EU fellows with visa and residence requirements, extendable to non-EU family members
eligibility: Doctorate obtained more than five years prior to the start of the fellowship on 1 September; to apply for 2027-28 the PhD should have been awarded before 1 September 2022
Open to post-docs, tenure-track academics and those wishing to spend their sabbatical at the Centre
Candidates of all nationalities are eligible for the Jean Monnet Fellowships
Research proposal should fit well with one of the Centre's main research themes, programmes and projects
Applicants who obtained their doctorate less than five years ago are directed to the EUI Max Weber Programme; it is not possible to apply for both
requirements: Research proposal (2-4 pages) in PDF, fitting one of the Centre's main research themes, programmes and projects
Curriculum vitae with a list of publications in PDF
Letter of motivation (1-2 pages) in PDF
Two letters of reference submitted online directly by the referees by the deadline
Residence in the area of Florence for the duration of the fellowship
The research done during the fellowship should lead to a publication, as an EUI Working Paper, in a scientific journal, or with a reputable academic publisher
Good knowledge of English, and of any other language relevant to the proposed research
documents: CV with a list of publications, PDF
Two reference letters submitted online by the referees, PDF
selection_criteria: The main criteria during the selection procedure are the CV of the applicant, the overall scientific quality of the proposal, and the fit of the proposal with the research programme of the RSCAS
Candidates are selected by the Academic Staff of the RSCAS and their nomination needs to be approved by the Executive Committee of the EUI
Applications are considered on the basis of application documents and references; there are no interviews
In case a reserve list is drawn up, places can be offered to reserve candidates if selected candidates do not accept the offer of a fellowship
coverage: The basic grant is EUR 2,850 per month
If the fellow receives other grants or salaries the amount of the fellowship will be fixed at a lower rate (minimum EUR 2,100 per month) depending on the amount of the additional income
A household allowance of up to EUR 310 per month is paid to fellows with a partner living with them in Florence, subject to a partner income under EUR 2,000 per month
A dependants allowance of EUR 210 per month for each dependent child living with the fellow in Florence; no allowance is paid for dependent children over the age of 26
All fellows are entitled to 650 EUR for eligible research expenses, such as attendance at conferences

Reimbursement of the incoming trip from the place of origin to Florence and the outgoing trip at the end of the fellowship; the maximum amount for travel reimbursement is EUR 1,200 including both trips, on a first-class rail or economy air basis
Reimbursement of visa-related costs (consular fees and travel to the nearest consulate) up to a maximum of EUR 250, on the basis of supporting documents
There is no provision for removal or installation expenses
The fellowship is not taxed by the Institute; fellows must comply with any other applicable tax provisions
Fellows must have adequate medical insurance cover, either through their own scheme or by subscribing to the EUI's private sickness and health insurance scheme at their own expense
application_method: Register the application as early as possible on the EUI OSIRIS portal (apply.eui.eu), process JMF_APPLY, inserting personal details and referee details
Complete the application details and upload the final versions of the attachments, then submit by the deadline of 23 October 2026 (14:00 CEST)
Two academic referees submit their reference letters online directly by the same deadline; references from current full-time or part-time EUI professors are not accepted
Letters sent through a dossier service such as Interfolio are accepted if the originals are sent to the EUI by the service and are not disclosed to the applicant
official.application_route: Apply online through the EUI OSIRIS portal (apply.eui.eu, process JMF_APPLY); register referee details early so both reference letters arrive before 23 October 2026, 14:00 CEST
official.study_mode: Residential; fellows must live in the area of Florence for the duration of the fellowship
official.citizenship_residency: Candidates of all nationalities are eligible; there is no citizenship or residency restriction
official.international_eligibility: Open to candidates of all nationalities; the EUI assists non-EU fellows with visa and residence requirements, and assistance can also be provided to their non-EU family members
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The research proposal should fit well with one of the Centre's main research themes, programmes and projects, whose programmes and chairs include the Florence School of Regulation, the Florence School of Banking and Finance, the Migration Policy Centre, the Centre for Media Pluralism and Media Freedom, the Centre for a Digital Society, the European Governance and Politics Programme, the Global Governance Programme, the Centre for Judicial Cooperation and the Tommaso Padoa-Schioppa, Pierre Werner and Ernst B. Haas chairs
official.research_requirement: A research proposal of 2-4 pages in PDF, judged on its overall scientific quality and its fit with the research programme of the RSCAS
official.duration: One year (12 months from September to August)
official.description: The Robert Schuman Centre for Advanced Studies offers one-year Jean Monnet Fellowships to scholars who have obtained their doctorate more than five years prior to the start of the fellowship, i.e. 1 September 2027 for the academic year 2027-28. Fellows are based at the Centre in Villa Schifanoia, are associated with one of the Centre's projects or programmes, and are expected to actively participate in the academic life of the Centre.
official.program_type: Senior postdoctoral research fellowship at an international research institute
official.english_requirement: No formal language test is published. The FAQ states that fellows should have a good knowledge of English, and of any other language relevant to their proposed research, and that the official working language of the postdoctoral programmes is English; documents in English guarantee the widest possible reading.

applicant_utility.summary: The Jean Monnet Fellowship pays a basic grant of EUR 2,850 a month for 12 months in Florence, plus EUR 650 for research expenses, travel reimbursement capped at EUR 1,200 and visa costs up to EUR 250. The single application is made through the EUI OSIRIS portal with a CV, a 1-2 page motivation letter, a 2-4 page research proposal and a passport scan, but the practical bottleneck is your two referees, whose letters must land by the same 23 October 2026 (14:00 CEST) cutoff. Selection turns on your CV, the scientific quality of the proposal and its fit with a named Robert Schuman Centre programme, with results emailed by the end of January.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career and senior scholars more than five years past their PhD whose current project maps onto a named RSCAS programme, centre or chair (regulation, banking and finance, migration, media pluralism, digital society, European or global governance, judicial cooperation) and who can commit to living in Florence for a full academic year.
application_readiness_checklist: Register on apply.eui.eu (process JMF_APPLY) and enter referee contact details as early as possible, ideally when the form opens in late July 2026, then email each referee to confirm they received the EUI request and will submit in time.
Check your PhD award date is before 1 September 2022; if it is later you belong in the Max Weber Programme instead and cannot apply to both in the same cycle.
Map the proposal explicitly to one named RSCAS programme, centre or chair so the 'fit with the research programme of the RSCAS' criterion is visible on the first page.
Produce flat files with standard international fonts: no macros, special characters, password protection or electronic signatures, and note that the passport must be a JPG rather than a PDF.
Arrange health cover and budget the items the grant does not touch, since insurance is at your own expense and there is no removal or installation allowance.
common_rejection_risks: Reference letters that arrive after 14:00 CEST on 23 October 2026; the dossier can be judged incomplete and references play an important part in the selection that begins immediately after the deadline.
A proposal that reads as generic European studies instead of being tied to a specific RSCAS programme or project, since fit with the Centre is an explicit criterion.
Nominating a current full-time or part-time EUI professor as a referee, whose reference will not be accepted.
Password-protected or non-standard-format documents, and dossier-service letters that are disclosed to the applicant rather than sent as originals to the EUI.
Letting generative AI write substantial parts of the motivation letter or proposal without acknowledging it, contrary to the EUI AI guidelines the call invokes.
Arriving after September or leaving before 20 July, which reduces or terminates the grant and forfeits the August payment.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Medical insurance (the EUI Cigna scheme or an equivalent policy at your own expense), removal and installation costs (explicitly not provided), travel for family members since only the fellow's incoming and outgoing trips are reimbursed, taxi costs, and any gap between Florence living costs and the monthly grant, which drops to a minimum of EUR 2,100 if you hold another grant or salary.
document_audit: The CV must carry a list of publications; a plain CV without the publication list is incomplete.
Length limits are hard: motivation letter 1-2 pages, research proposal 2-4 pages, both PDF.
The passport copy is the one required file in JPG format, not PDF.
Exactly two references are requested and accepted, so a third letter will not be looked at.
If you use Interfolio or a similar service, the original letters must reach the EUI directly and must not be disclosed to you.
Family allowances require supporting documents such as marriage or cohabitation proof and birth certificates, plus school or university certificates for children over 18 in full-time education.
alerts: The deadline is a hard portal cutoff: after 23 October 2026 (14:00 CEST) the online application form is no longer active.
Holding another grant or salary cuts the monthly fellowship to a minimum of EUR 2,100, and it must be disclosed to the EUI with supporting documents.
The selection decision is final and not subject to appeal, and no individual feedback is given on proposals that are not selected.
Reserve-list places are only offered if selected candidates decline, so an early offer email from the EUI should be answered quickly.
Polish candidates are automatically considered for the single Jean Monnet Fellowship funded by the Polish Ministry of Science and Higher Education through the same application.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register early on apply.eui.eu with referee details, complete and upload the four files, submit before 23 October 2026 (14:00 CEST), then chase both referees until their letters are uploaded by the same deadline.
